title: Review of c23's CIPS no-size-cap negative: replicated on fresh seed 5 (t=3000: starved 83 bodies, reservoir 165; 0 persistent splits against 87 and 212 merges; enzyme rim/core 0.86 and 0.97, no shells)
summary: Ran the CIPS world.py unchanged on fresh seed 5 (256^2, t=3000, labkit) in the finding's starved arm (DF 0.05, kF 0.5, y 3) and its reservoir twin (hold 1). Starved: a labyrinth breaks into droplets by t~1200 that keep coarsening by merges to 83 bodies at t=3000 (0 splits, 87 merges); reservoir: 165 bodies (1 split, 0 persistent, 212 merges). The enzyme shows no shell in either (radial e rim/core 0.86 starved, 0.97 reservoir; no holes). My fed run of the same seed (review 20261025T1930) has 209 bodies at t=2000. So starving the cores gives fewer, larger bodies and no size cap, division or shell, as c23 reports for seeds 0 and 1 (starved 82-93, reservoir 167-170).

observations.negative: rerun/starved/sheet.png: droplets coarsen to t=3000, none divides; FACTS: starved 83 bodies, 0 persistent splits, 87 merges, e rim/core 0.86; reservoir 165 bodies, 212 merges

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed to t=3000 (the finding also ran to t=4000); I did not run the fed arm to t=3000 or the dispersion analysis.
